whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of the fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases. That means your recovery isn't artificially capped just because your injuries are hard to put a dollar figure on.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to have your case reviewed or handled. Fees only come out of money recovered on your behalf.

items.question: Do I have a case if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than denied outright. We can help sort out how fault might apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Woodlake?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity or road, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking early.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Woodlake?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reports cluster on corridors like Avenue 344, Valencia Boulevard, Rt 216, and Main Street, with activity often peaking on Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m. These are simply the counts on record, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe anything if I contact you?
items.answer: No. We provide free case reviews, and we work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: What if my injuries seem minor right now?
items.answer: Some injuries, like whiplash or concussions, don't show their full impact until days or weeks later. It's still worth having a conversation about what happened while details and evidence are fresh.
